units: <cite ref="Berakhot 14b:24">Ber. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>כאילו מעיד ע׳ וכ׳</he> as if offering evidence of falsehood against himself.
<cite ref="Sukkah 29a:14">Succ. 29ᵃ</cite> <he>מעידי ע׳ שקר</he> those who give false witness.

<cite ref="Shabbat 22b:2">Sabb. 22ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 24:3">Lev. XXIV, 3</cite>) <he>ע׳ היא לבאי עולם וכ׳</he> it (the light in the Temple) is an evidence to mankind that the Divine Presence dwells in Israel; <cite ref="Menachot 86b:8">Men. 86ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Menachot 86b:10">Ib.</cite> <he>מאי עֵדוּתָהּ</he> how did it give evidence (of the Divine Presence)?; Sabb. l. c. <he>מאי עדות</he> (corr. acc., as Ms. M.).
<cite ref="Makkot 5a:8">Macc. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>גופה של ע׳</he> (not <he>עדיות</he>) the testimony to the fact itself, v. <cite ref="O01595"><he>סָרָה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Makkot 1:7">Ib. I, 7</cite> <he>אם מתקיימת הע׳ בשנים וכ׳</he> if an evidence is legally established by two witnesses, why does the Scripture mention three? <cite ref="Mishnah Makkot 1:8">Ib. 8</cite> <he>מה שנים … עֵדוּתָן בטלה וכ׳</he> as in the case of two witnesses, if one of them is found out to be a relative or a disqualified witness, their testimony is void, so in the case of three &c.—

Ex. R. s. 41 מה כלה … כל מי שיודע לי ע׳ וכ׳ as the bride … on entering her chamber (in procession) uncovers her face, as if saying, whoever knows any evidence against me, let him come …, so must the scholar &c.; Yalk. ib. 391; Cant. R. to IV, 11 וזו עֵדוּתִי מעידה עלי and this (procession) is my testimonial testifying for me; a. v. fr.—Trnsf. (v. סַהֲדוּ) tokens of virginity.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 60">Gen. R. s. 60</cite> <he>ממקום עֵדוּתָן</he> Ar. (ed. <he>ערותן</he>) at the seat of virginity.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 45">Gen. R. s. 45</cite>; s. 51 <he>הוציאו עדותן</he> Ar. (ed.; Yalk. ib. 79 <he>ערותן</he>).—Pl. <he>עֵדָיוֹת</he>.

Macc. I, 9 הרי אלו שתי ע׳ these are two testimonies (two independent sets of witnesses); a. fr.—‘Eduyoth, name of a treatise, of the Order of N’ziḳin, of the Mishnah and Tosefta, containing statements of traditional deliveries and rules.
Ber. 28ᵃ ע׳ בו ביום נשנית on that day ‘Eduyoth was taught.
